..
Issued at 201 PM EDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast:

Longwave upper level ridging continues to build slowly east into the 
western Great Lakes early this afternoon, with its surface 
reflection running just a bit ahead of it...currently centered right 
across lower Michigan. Result is plenty of sunshine across the 
Northwoods, with all that sun helping boost temperatures to about 
early August specific normal values in the 70s to lower 80s. 
Expanding the regional view shows shortwave troughing and attendant 
weak surface low/troughing pivoting steadily east across the 
northern Rockies and into the northern Plains...kicking off some 
scattered convection in the process across that area.

Overall pattern remains somewhat a progressive one heading through 
the period, with current overhead high pressure gradually sliding 
off to the east...allowing upstream wave to pivot into and across 
our area during the middle of the week. Still appears northern 
Michigan becomes centered within broad low amplitude troughing 
regime between west Atlantic and southwest Conus ridge axes to end 
the week on into the start of the weekend. Large scale regime may 
attempt to relax a bit thereafter, allowing more zonal central NOAM 
upper level flow to develop into early next week.   

Primary Forecast Concerns:

Temperature trends through the period and addressing periodic rain 
chances...especially those centered on the mid-week period.

Details: 

While slowly sliding off to the east, expect high pressure to remain 
in control of our weather tonight into at least the first half of 
Tuesday. Another somewhat chilly night tonight, with light winds and 
clear skies driving a good nocturnal temperature response. Evening 
will start a bit warmer, so expect readings to stay just a bit above 
those observed last night. Still...would expect another night of 
widespread 50s, with some of our traditional ice box locations in 
the Au Sable River Valley perhaps making a run at the upper 40s. 
These readings will probably be just cold enough to entice the 
development of some "field" fog and fog near inland bodies of water, 
but definitely shouldn't be a big deal at all.

Dry conditions continue through much of Tuesday. By late in the day 
may see some broken convection make a run at eastern upper 
Michigan/northern Lake Michigan right along and a bit ahead of that 
next wave/weak cold front. Definitely not expecting anything 
significant given only a few hundred joules/kg of most unstable cape 
and with better shear profiles detached to the west. Moisture 
convergence axis will continue to work slowly east into the area 
Tuesday night. Despite unfavorable timing, increasing right entrance 
region upper jet support and continued deep layer moisture advection 
should help gradually expand shower coverage with time. Again, lack 
of instabilty should keep any embedded thunderstorms below severe 
limits. May see some pockets of heavier rain totals with rather 
saturated conditions through the vertical (precipitable water values 
exceed 1.75 inches) and expected relatively slow southeast 
progression of showers/storms. This idea continues into Wednesday, 
with better chances for rain centering toward Saginaw Bay and points 
southwest with time. Do think exit of rain will be a bit faster than 
currently advertised by some guidance Wednesday night as corridor of 
upper jet support exits and congealed cold pools push axis of 
enhanced low level convergence into southern Michigan. Much of the 
area does remain under marginal risk wording for excessive rain 
Tuesday night into Wednesday night. Belief is any heavy rain will be 
localized at best, with the much better heavy rain potential 
remaining well off to our southwest. A bit warm for Tuesday, with 
highs mostly in the upper 70s to middle 80s. A tad cooler for 
Wednesday behind the passing front and with clouds/showers.

Not seeing anything real significant for the remainder of the 
period. Does look like a slow warming trend, with highs Friday 
through the weekend mostly in the 80s. Any passing waves may help 
kick off a few showers and storms at times, but again current trends 
support nothing of any real significance. Plenty of time to work all 
those details out in the coming days.
